---
title: "RNA-seq Comprehensive Concept Quiz"
subtitle: "Concept review before the hands-on Shell and R sessions"
author: "Krushna Chandra Murmu"
institute: "Bioinformatics Specialist, Premas Life Sciences"

format:
  revealjs:
    theme: simple
    width: 1600
    height: 900
    margin: 0.045
    center: false
    progress: true
    controls: true
    navigation-mode: linear
    transition: fade
    background-transition: fade
    toc: false
    scrollable: true
    quiz:
      allowNumberKeys: true
      disableOnCheck: true
      disableReset: true
      shuffleOptions: true
      defaultCorrect: "Correct"
      defaultIncorrect: "Incorrect"
      includeScore: true
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
        :root {
          --blue: #165DAD;
          --dark: #10243E;
          --soft: #F3F7FB;
          --border: #D8E4F0;
          --green: #2F855A;
          --warm: #FFF7E8;
          --red: #C53030;
        }

        .reveal { font-size: 32px; }
        .reveal h1 { color: var(--dark); font-size: 1.9em; }
        .reveal h2 {
          color: var(--dark);
          font-size: 1.35em;
          border-bottom: 3px solid #d7e3f1;
          padding-bottom: .12em;
        }

        .reveal .slides section {
          max-height: 900px;
          overflow-y: auto !important;
          overflow-x: hidden;
          padding: 12px 28px;
          box-sizing: border-box;
        }

        .takehome-card {
          border: 1px solid var(--border);
          border-left: 9px solid var(--green);
          border-radius: 14px;
          background: #F5FAF6;
          padding: 18px 22px;
          margin: 14px 0;
        }

        /* Make quiz options projector-friendly */
        .quiz-question li.option-button {
          font-size: 0.88em;
          line-height: 1.25;
          margin: 11px 0;
          padding: 12px 16px !important;
          border-radius: 10px;
        }

        /*
          IMPORTANT:
          Individual quiz slides do NOT show Check, Reset, or running score.
          Participants commit all answers first.
        */
        .quiz-question .check-button,
        .quiz-question .reset-button,
        .quiz-question .score {
          display: none !important;
        }

        .quiz-question .button-container {
          margin-top: 16px;
        }

        /* Keep only navigation buttons visible on question slides */
        .quiz-question .prev-button,
        .quiz-question .next-button {
          font-size: 0.72em;
          padding: 7px 14px;
        }

        /* Correct answers are shown only after final submission */
        body.quiz-review-mode .quiz-question li.review-correct-answer {
          outline: 4px solid #2F855A !important;
          background: #E6F6EC !important;
          position: relative;
        }

        body.quiz-review-mode .quiz-question li.review-correct-answer::after {
          content: "  ✓ Correct answer";
          font-weight: 800;
          color: #206A42;
        }

        #quiz-submit-panel {
          max-width: 1050px;
          margin: 32px auto 0 auto;
          text-align: center;
          padding: 26px 30px;
          border: 1px solid var(--border);
          border-radius: 18px;
          background: var(--soft);
          box-shadow: 0 5px 18px rgba(16,36,62,.10);
        }

        #submit-final-quiz,
        #review-final-quiz {
          font-size: 0.80em;
          font-weight: 700;
          border: 0;
          border-radius: 10px;
          padding: 12px 22px;
          margin: 10px 8px;
          cursor: pointer;
        }

        #submit-final-quiz {
          background: var(--blue);
          color: white;
        }

        #review-final-quiz {
          background: #E6F6EC;
          color: #206A42;
          border: 2px solid #8FD0A8;
          display: none;
        }

        #quiz-final-message {
          margin-top: 16px;
          font-size: 1.02em;
          font-weight: 700;
          color: var(--dark);
        }

        #quiz-final-score {
          font-size: 1.65em;
          font-weight: 800;
          color: var(--blue);
          margin-top: 16px;
        }

        .quiz-small-note {
          font-size: 0.70em;
          color: #52677D;
        }
        </style>

revealjs-plugins:
  - quiz

include-after-body:
  text: |
    <script>
    (function () {
      function setupFinalOnlyQuiz() {
        if (!window.Reveal || typeof window.Reveal.on !== "function") {
          setTimeout(setupFinalOnlyQuiz, 100);
          return;
        }

        function getQuizSlides() {
          return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("section.quiz-question"));
        }

        function answered(slide) {
          return slide.querySelectorAll("li.option-button.selected").length > 0;
        }

        function revealCorrectAnswers() {
          document.body.classList.add("quiz-review-mode");

          getQuizSlides().forEach(function (slide) {
            slide.querySelectorAll("li.option-button").forEach(function (li) {
              const correctSpan = li.querySelector("span.correct");
              if (correctSpan) {
                li.classList.add("review-correct-answer");
              }
            });
          });
        }

        function gradeQuiz() {
          const slides = getQuizSlides();
          const unanswered = slides.filter(function (slide) {
            return !answered(slide);
          });

          const message = document.getElementById("quiz-final-message");
          const scoreBox = document.getElementById("quiz-final-score");
          const reviewBtn = document.getElementById("review-final-quiz");

          if (unanswered.length > 0) {
            message.textContent =
              "You still have " + unanswered.length +
              " unanswered question" + (unanswered.length === 1 ? "." : "s.");
            scoreBox.textContent = "";
            return;
          }

          /*
            Trigger the extension's own grading only now.
            Until this point participants cannot check individual questions.
          */
          slides.forEach(function (slide) {
            const check = slide.querySelector(".check-button");
            if (check && !check.disabled) {
              check.click();
            }
          });

          /*
            quarto-quiz updates its hidden score on every quiz slide.
            Read the first one after grading.
          */
          setTimeout(function () {
            const hiddenScore = document.querySelector(
              "section.quiz-question .score"
            );

            const scoreText = hiddenScore
              ? hiddenScore.textContent
              : "Quiz submitted";

            scoreBox.textContent = scoreText;
            message.textContent =
              "Quiz submitted. Your answers are now locked.";

            reviewBtn.style.display = "inline-block";
          }, 100);
        }

        document.addEventListener("click", function (event) {
          if (event.target && event.target.id === "submit-final-quiz") {
            gradeQuiz();
          }

          if (event.target && event.target.id === "review-final-quiz") {
            revealCorrectAnswers();

            const firstQuiz = getQuizSlides()[0];
            if (firstQuiz) {
              const indices = window.Reveal.getIndices(firstQuiz);
              window.Reveal.slide(indices.h, indices.v || 0);
            }
          }
        });
      }

      setupFinalOnlyQuiz();
    })();
    </script>

editor: source
---

# RNA-seq Comprehensive Concept Quiz

## How this quiz works

::: {.takehome-card}
### One submission at the end

Choose your answers as you move through the questions.

**You will not see whether an answer is correct or incorrect while answering.**

At the end, select **Submit Quiz & Show Score**.

Only after the score is calculated will **Review Correct Answers** become available.
:::

- Number keys can be used to select options.
- Multi-select questions are labeled **Select all that apply**.
- You may move backward and change answers **before final submission**.
- Once submitted, answers are locked.

---

# Section 1 — RNA-seq Foundations

## 1. What does bulk RNA-seq primarily measure? {.quiz-question}

- [The relative abundance of RNA-derived sequencing fragments across a biological sample]{.correct data-explanation="Bulk RNA-seq samples RNA-derived fragments from the whole specimen and measures their abundance collectively."}
- [The exact number of intact RNA molecules in every cell]{data-explanation="Bulk RNA-seq does not directly count intact molecules in individual cells."}
- [Only DNA sequence variants]{data-explanation="DNA variant detection is not the primary purpose of standard bulk RNA-seq expression analysis."}
- [Protein abundance directly]{data-explanation="RNA-seq measures RNA-derived sequence abundance, not protein abundance directly."}

---

## 2. Which are important RNA-seq library-design choices? {.quiz-question .quiz-multiple}

**Select all that apply.**

- [Poly(A) selection versus rRNA depletion]{.correct data-explanation="This choice changes which RNA populations are represented in the library."}
- [Stranded versus unstranded library preparation]{.correct data-explanation="Strandedness affects how reads can be assigned to overlapping transcripts and genes."}
- [Single-end versus paired-end sequencing]{.correct data-explanation="Read configuration affects mapping and fragment-level information."}
- [The color used for the PCA plot]{data-explanation="Plot styling is not a library-preparation choice."}

---

## 3. Why are biological replicates important? {.quiz-question}

- [They capture biological variability and support inference beyond a single specimen]{.correct data-explanation="Biological replication allows variability among independent biological units to be estimated."}
- [They make FASTQ quality scores larger]{data-explanation="Replication does not alter sequencing quality-score definitions."}
- [They eliminate all batch effects automatically]{data-explanation="Replicates do not automatically remove confounding or batch effects."}
- [They replace the need for metadata]{data-explanation="Metadata remain essential for describing experimental structure."}

---

## 4. Which situation represents confounding? {.quiz-question}

- [All controls are processed in Batch 1 and all treated samples in Batch 2]{.correct data-explanation="Condition and batch cannot be separated because they change together."}
- [Controls and treated samples are balanced across both batches]{data-explanation="Balancing condition across batches helps separate condition from batch effects."}
- [Each condition contains independent biological replicates]{data-explanation="Replication is desirable and does not by itself create confounding."}
- [Sample metadata record both condition and batch]{data-explanation="Recording covariates supports appropriate modeling; it is not itself confounding."}

---

# Section 2 — FASTQ and Quality Control

## 5. What information is contained in a FASTQ record? {.quiz-question}

- [Read identifier, nucleotide sequence and per-base quality information]{.correct data-explanation="FASTQ stores a read identifier, sequence, separator and encoded per-base quality scores."}
- [Gene counts and adjusted p-values]{data-explanation="Those belong to downstream count and statistical result tables."}
- [Only chromosome coordinates]{data-explanation="Chromosome coordinates are produced after alignment."}
- [Gene Ontology categories]{data-explanation="GO categories are used during downstream functional interpretation."}

---

## 6. What does a Phred Q30 base quality indicate? {.quiz-question}

- [An estimated base-call error probability of about 0.001]{.correct data-explanation="Q30 corresponds to an estimated error probability of 10^-3, or roughly one error per thousand base calls."}
- [A 30% probability that the base is wrong]{data-explanation="Q30 is logarithmic and corresponds to a much smaller error probability."}
- [A mapping quality of exactly 30]{data-explanation="Base quality and mapping quality are different concepts."}
- [Thirty reads mapped to one gene]{data-explanation="Phred quality does not describe read counts."}

---

## 7. Which are typical raw-read QC checks? {.quiz-question .quiz-multiple}

**Select all that apply.**

- [Per-base sequence quality]{.correct data-explanation="Base-quality profiles are a standard FASTQ QC metric."}
- [Adapter content]{.correct data-explanation="Adapter contamination can indicate short inserts or incomplete trimming."}
- [GC distribution]{.correct data-explanation="Unexpected GC profiles can indicate contamination or library-specific effects."}
- [Adjusted p-value distribution]{data-explanation="Adjusted p-values are generated much later during statistical testing."}

---

## 8. A FastQC warning should generally be interpreted as what? {.quiz-question}

- [A diagnostic signal that should be interpreted in the context of the library and experiment]{.correct data-explanation="FastQC warnings are flags for investigation and are not automatically reasons to discard data."}
- [Proof that the sample must be deleted]{data-explanation="Warnings require interpretation and do not automatically imply unusable data."}
- [Proof that alignment will fail]{data-explanation="Many warnings do not prevent successful alignment."}
- [Evidence that DESeq2 normalization is wrong]{data-explanation="FASTQ QC occurs before DESeq2 and does not directly diagnose DESeq2 normalization."}

---

# Section 3 — Alignment and Reference Files

## 9. Why does RNA-seq usually require a splice-aware aligner? {.quiz-question}

- [RNA-derived reads can span exon-exon junctions that are separated by introns in the genome]{.correct data-explanation="Splice-aware aligners can represent split alignments across genomic introns."}
- [RNA reads never contain sequencing errors]{data-explanation="RNA-seq reads can contain sequencing errors like other sequencing reads."}
- [RNA-seq does not use a reference sequence]{data-explanation="Genome-based RNA-seq alignment typically uses a reference genome."}
- [Every RNA read maps to several chromosomes]{data-explanation="Multi-mapping can occur, but it is not the defining reason for splice-aware alignment."}

---

## 10. What is the main role of a reference FASTA? {.quiz-question}

- [To provide the nucleotide sequence against which reads are aligned]{.correct data-explanation="The FASTA contains the reference sequence used to locate reads."}
- [To describe gene and exon coordinates]{data-explanation="Feature coordinates are generally supplied through GTF or GFF annotation files."}
- [To store sample condition labels]{data-explanation="Sample conditions belong in metadata."}
- [To contain differential-expression statistics]{data-explanation="Statistical results are produced downstream."}

---

## 11. What is the main role of a GTF/GFF annotation? {.quiz-question}

- [To describe genomic features such as genes, transcripts and exons]{.correct data-explanation="Annotations connect genomic coordinates to biological features and identifiers."}
- [To store compressed raw reads]{data-explanation="Raw sequencing reads are typically stored as FASTQ or FASTQ.GZ."}
- [To contain only base-quality scores]{data-explanation="Base-quality scores belong to FASTQ."}
- [To replace the reference genome sequence]{data-explanation="Annotation complements rather than replaces the reference sequence."}

---

## 12. Why must FASTA and GTF/GFF versions be compatible? {.quiz-question}

- [Their genome build and chromosome coordinate system must refer to the same reference]{.correct data-explanation="Build or chromosome-name mismatches can disrupt annotation, counting and interpretation."}
- [Both files must contain identical text]{data-explanation="They contain different types of information."}
- [Both must have the same file extension]{data-explanation="Biological compatibility is not determined by file extension."}
- [DESeq2 requires both files directly]{data-explanation="DESeq2 normally uses a count matrix and sample metadata."}

---

## 13. What does a high MAPQ generally represent? {.quiz-question}

- [Greater confidence in the genomic placement of the read]{.correct data-explanation="Mapping quality summarizes confidence that the read has been placed at the correct location."}
- [Greater confidence in every nucleotide base call]{data-explanation="Per-base confidence is represented by base quality, not MAPQ."}
- [A larger gene fold change]{data-explanation="MAPQ is an alignment metric, not a differential-expression effect size."}
- [More enriched pathways]{data-explanation="Pathway enrichment is unrelated to individual alignment MAPQ."}

---

## 14. What commonly causes multi-mapping? {.quiz-question .quiz-multiple}

**Select all that apply.**

- [Repetitive genomic sequence]{.correct data-explanation="Repeated sequence can provide multiple equally plausible alignment locations."}
- [Highly similar paralogous genes]{.correct data-explanation="Closely related genes can contain sequence that cannot be uniquely assigned."}
- [Pseudogenes with sequence similarity]{.correct data-explanation="Pseudogene similarity can create ambiguous mapping."}
- [Using an adjusted p-value threshold]{data-explanation="Statistical thresholds are unrelated to alignment ambiguity."}

---

# Section 4 — SAM/BAM and Counting

## 15. What is the key difference between SAM and BAM? {.quiz-question}

- [BAM is a compressed binary representation of SAM alignment information]{.correct data-explanation="SAM is text-based and human-readable, while BAM stores equivalent alignment records in binary form."}
- [SAM stores genes while BAM stores proteins]{data-explanation="Both are sequence-alignment formats."}
- [SAM is RNA-only and BAM is DNA-only]{data-explanation="Both formats are used across sequencing applications."}
- [BAM is an annotation format]{data-explanation="BAM stores alignments, not gene annotation definitions."}

---

## 16. In `50M1000N50M`, what does the `N` represent in RNA-seq? {.quiz-question}

- [Reference sequence skipped by a spliced alignment, commonly an intron]{.correct data-explanation="N is used for skipped reference regions and is characteristic of splice-aware RNA-seq alignments."}
- [A base with an unknown quality score]{data-explanation="CIGAR N does not encode sequencing-quality values."}
- [A duplicated read]{data-explanation="Duplicate status is encoded elsewhere in alignment metadata."}
- [A gene with no expression]{data-explanation="CIGAR operations describe read-to-reference alignment structure."}

---

## 17. Which operations are commonly performed with SAMtools? {.quiz-question .quiz-multiple}

**Select all that apply.**

- [Sorting alignment files]{.correct data-explanation="Coordinate sorting is a common SAMtools workflow step."}
- [Indexing BAM files]{.correct data-explanation="BAM indexes support rapid access to genomic regions."}
- [Viewing and filtering alignment records]{.correct data-explanation="SAMtools can inspect or filter SAM/BAM records."}
- [Performing GO over-representation analysis]{data-explanation="GO enrichment is a downstream functional-analysis task."}

---

## 18. Why is coordinate sorting useful? {.quiz-question}

- [It places alignments in genomic order and supports efficient indexed access]{.correct data-explanation="Coordinate-sorted BAM files are required or preferred by many downstream genomic tools."}
- [It alphabetically sorts gene symbols for enrichment]{data-explanation="Coordinate sorting acts on alignment positions, not functional-analysis gene symbols."}
- [It normalizes library sizes]{data-explanation="Library normalization occurs during downstream count analysis."}
- [It calculates p-values]{data-explanation="Sorting is a file-processing operation, not a statistical test."}

---

## 19. What does featureCounts conceptually do? {.quiz-question}

- [Assigns aligned reads or fragments to annotated genomic features]{.correct data-explanation="featureCounts overlaps alignments with annotation features to generate feature-level counts."}
- [Performs splice-aware alignment from FASTQ]{data-explanation="Alignment happens before featureCounts."}
- [Performs differential-expression hypothesis testing]{data-explanation="Statistical testing occurs after gene counts are generated."}
- [Builds a genome FASTA]{data-explanation="Reference genome construction is not the role of featureCounts."}

---

## 20. Which factors can change feature assignment? {.quiz-question .quiz-multiple}

**Select all that apply.**

- [Library strandedness]{.correct data-explanation="Strand assumptions can change whether an overlapping alignment is compatible with a gene."}
- [Single-end versus paired-end counting rules]{.correct data-explanation="Paired-end libraries are often counted at the fragment rather than individual-read level."}
- [Ambiguous overlap with multiple genomic features]{.correct data-explanation="Ambiguous overlaps may remain unassigned or be handled according to counting rules."}
- [Volcano-plot point size]{data-explanation="Plot styling has no effect on gene assignment."}

---

# Section 5 — Count Matrix and Statistical Modeling

## 21. What should DESeq2 or edgeR typically receive as expression input? {.quiz-question}

- [Raw integer-like gene counts]{.correct data-explanation="Count-based negative-binomial methods are designed around raw count observations with internal normalization."}
- [Only TPM values]{data-explanation="TPM is useful for some abundance comparisons but is not the standard input to these count-based differential-expression models."}
- [Only FPKM values]{data-explanation="FPKM is not the expected count input for standard DESeq2 or edgeR testing."}
- [Only z-scores]{data-explanation="Z-scores do not preserve the count-distribution assumptions used by these models."}

---

## 22. Why not compare raw counts directly between samples? {.quiz-question}

- [Observed counts are influenced by library size, sampling and biological variability]{.correct data-explanation="Raw counts reflect more than biological expression and require an appropriate statistical model."}
- [Raw counts cannot contain zeros]{data-explanation="RNA-seq count matrices commonly contain zeros."}
- [Raw counts are always normally distributed]{data-explanation="Count data are discrete and commonly show mean-dependent variance and overdispersion."}
- [Raw counts already represent adjusted p-values]{data-explanation="Counts and p-values are completely different quantities."}

---

## 23. What is the null hypothesis for a standard gene-level condition test? {.quiz-question}

- [There is no systematic condition effect on expression for that gene]{.correct data-explanation="The null usually corresponds to a zero condition coefficient or no expression difference attributable to the tested condition."}
- [The gene has exactly zero reads in all samples]{data-explanation="A gene can be expressed while still showing no condition effect."}
- [Every sample must have identical counts]{data-explanation="Counts can vary among replicates even under the null."}
- [All genes are differentially expressed]{data-explanation="The test is gene-specific and the null represents no tested effect."}

---

## 24. Why is the negative binomial model useful for RNA-seq? {.quiz-question}

- [It can represent count data with variability greater than expected under a simple Poisson model]{.correct data-explanation="RNA-seq biological replicates commonly show overdispersion, which the negative binomial can model."}
- [It assumes every gene has the same count]{data-explanation="The model allows gene-specific means and dispersion behavior."}
- [It converts BAM files to FASTQ]{data-explanation="That is a file-format operation unrelated to count modeling."}
- [It performs pathway annotation]{data-explanation="Pathway annotation occurs downstream of statistical testing."}

---

## 25. What does dispersion represent conceptually? {.quiz-question}

- [Extra variability in counts around their expected mean]{.correct data-explanation="Dispersion captures biological and other variability beyond simple sampling noise."}
- [The chromosome position of a gene]{data-explanation="Genomic position is annotation information, not dispersion."}
- [The number of GO terms assigned to a gene]{data-explanation="Functional annotation is unrelated to count-model dispersion."}
- [The proportion of mapped reads]{data-explanation="Mapping rate is an alignment QC metric."}

---

## 26. Why do methods borrow information across genes when estimating dispersion? {.quiz-question}

- [Gene-wise variability estimates can be unstable, especially with limited replicates]{.correct data-explanation="Cross-gene information stabilizes noisy dispersion estimates and improves inference."}
- [All genes are assumed to have identical expression]{data-explanation="Borrowing information does not mean forcing identical expression across genes."}
- [It removes the need for biological replicates]{data-explanation="Replication remains fundamental for estimating biological variability."}
- [It guarantees every gene becomes significant]{data-explanation="Stabilization improves estimation; it does not guarantee significance."}

---

# Section 6 — DESeq2 and edgeR

## 27. Which pairing correctly matches common normalization strategies? {.quiz-question}

- [DESeq2: median-of-ratios; edgeR: TMM]{.correct data-explanation="These are the commonly used default scaling approaches in the two frameworks."}
- [DESeq2: TMM; edgeR: TPM]{data-explanation="TMM is commonly associated with edgeR, while TPM is not its standard count-model normalization."}
- [DESeq2: FPKM; edgeR: RPKM]{data-explanation="Neither uses FPKM/RPKM as its standard count-model normalization."}
- [DESeq2: quantile normalization; edgeR: z-score scaling]{data-explanation="These are not their usual count-model scaling strategies."}

---

## 28. What do DESeq2 and edgeR have in common? {.quiz-question .quiz-multiple}

**Select all that apply.**

- [They model gene counts using negative-binomial frameworks]{.correct data-explanation="Both are built around negative-binomial count models."}
- [They estimate dispersion for RNA-seq count variability]{.correct data-explanation="Dispersion estimation is central to both frameworks."}
- [They support generalized linear-model designs]{.correct data-explanation="Both can represent multifactor experimental designs through GLM frameworks."}
- [They require TPM as the statistical model input]{data-explanation="Both generally use raw gene counts for their count-based models."}

---

## 29. Which testing strategies are correctly associated with the packages? {.quiz-question .quiz-multiple}

**Select all that apply.**

- [DESeq2 commonly uses Wald tests for coefficients and contrasts]{.correct data-explanation="The Wald test is the standard DESeq2 testing approach for many contrasts."}
- [DESeq2 supports likelihood-ratio tests for nested models]{.correct data-explanation="DESeq2 can compare full and reduced models with an LRT."}
- [edgeR supports quasi-likelihood inference]{.correct data-explanation="edgeR provides quasi-likelihood GLM methods for robust inference."}
- [edgeR performs differential expression only with a t-test]{data-explanation="edgeR is based on negative-binomial count models, not a simple t-test-only framework."}

---

## 30. What is the main difference between effect size and statistical evidence? {.quiz-question}

- [Effect size describes the magnitude of change; p-values describe evidence against a null model]{.correct data-explanation="Fold change and statistical evidence answer different questions and should be interpreted together."}
- [They are two names for the same number]{data-explanation="Effect magnitude and hypothesis-test evidence are distinct quantities."}
- [Adjusted p-value indicates whether expression increased or decreased]{data-explanation="Direction is represented by the sign of the estimated effect, such as log2 fold change."}
- [Effect size depends only on the number of tested genes]{data-explanation="Effect size estimates the magnitude of a biological contrast, not the number of tests."}

---

# Section 7 — Multiple Testing and Interpretation

## 31. Why is multiple-testing correction required? {.quiz-question}

- [Testing thousands of genes creates many opportunities for chance-positive results]{.correct data-explanation="FDR-controlling procedures account for the multiplicity of genome-scale hypothesis testing."}
- [It increases every fold change]{data-explanation="Multiple-testing correction modifies statistical significance measures, not fold-change estimates."}
- [It changes FASTQ quality scores]{data-explanation="FASTQ base quality is unrelated to multiple-testing correction."}
- [It improves genome alignment]{data-explanation="Alignment occurs before differential-expression hypothesis testing."}

---

## 32. What does an FDR-controlled adjusted p-value help control? {.quiz-question}

- [The expected proportion of false discoveries among reported discoveries under the procedure]{.correct data-explanation="FDR procedures target false discoveries among the set called significant."}
- [The probability that every significant gene is biologically important]{data-explanation="Statistical significance is not identical to biological importance."}
- [The fraction of reads that map uniquely]{data-explanation="Unique mapping rate is an alignment QC metric."}
- [The number of transcripts in the annotation]{data-explanation="Annotation content is unrelated to FDR control."}

---

## 33. Which result deserves the most careful interpretation? {.quiz-question}

- [A statistically significant gene with a very small effect size]{.correct data-explanation="Statistical evidence does not automatically imply a biologically meaningful effect; magnitude and context matter."}
- [A gene whose sample-level pattern agrees with the modeled contrast]{data-explanation="Agreement between model and sample-level pattern strengthens interpretability."}
- [A pathway supported by several coherent genes]{data-explanation="Coherent multi-gene support can strengthen biological interpretation."}
- [A result that is consistent across independent replicates]{data-explanation="Consistency across biological replicates generally supports confidence in the observed pattern."}

---

# Section 8 — Visualization and Functional Analysis

## 34. What is PCA mainly used to assess in RNA-seq? {.quiz-question}

- [Global sample relationships and major sources of expression variation]{.correct data-explanation="PCA summarizes high-dimensional expression variation into major axes for sample-level exploration."}
- [The exact CIGAR string of each read]{data-explanation="CIGAR strings are alignment-record fields."}
- [Gene Ontology term definitions]{data-explanation="GO is a functional annotation system."}
- [FASTQ adapter sequences]{data-explanation="Adapter content is assessed during raw-read QC."}

---

## 35. What does an MA plot combine? {.quiz-question}

- [Mean abundance and log fold change]{.correct data-explanation="The MA plot shows expression effect size against average abundance."}
- [Mapping quality and base quality]{data-explanation="Those are sequencing/alignment quality metrics, not MA axes."}
- [GO term size and pathway score]{data-explanation="Those belong to enrichment visualization."}
- [Chromosome and genomic position]{data-explanation="Those would describe genome coordinates rather than an MA plot."}

---

## 36. What does a volcano plot emphasize? {.quiz-question}

- [Effect size together with statistical evidence]{.correct data-explanation="Volcano plots commonly place fold change on the x-axis and a significance measure on the y-axis."}
- [FASTQ quality versus GC content]{data-explanation="Those are raw-read QC measures."}
- [Genomic position versus MAPQ]{data-explanation="Those are alignment-related quantities."}
- [Transcript length versus exon count]{data-explanation="Those are annotation properties."}

---

## 37. What is the core difference between ORA and GSEA? {.quiz-question}

- [ORA uses a selected gene list; GSEA evaluates genes along a ranked list]{.correct data-explanation="ORA relies on a threshold-defined set, whereas GSEA looks for coordinated enrichment across a ranking."}
- [ORA uses FASTQ and GSEA uses BAM]{data-explanation="Both methods operate downstream on gene-level results."}
- [ORA performs alignment and GSEA performs counting]{data-explanation="Neither method performs primary sequencing analysis."}
- [ORA is only for DNA-seq]{data-explanation="ORA is widely used for gene-list interpretation in RNA-seq and other omics analyses."}

---

## 38. Why does the ORA background matter? {.quiz-question}

- [It defines the gene universe against which enrichment is evaluated]{.correct data-explanation="The chosen universe changes the expected overlap and therefore the enrichment statistics."}
- [It determines FASTQ compression]{data-explanation="Compression is unrelated to functional enrichment statistics."}
- [It replaces the selected significant gene list]{data-explanation="ORA requires both a selected set and an appropriate background universe."}
- [It sets BAM coordinate order]{data-explanation="BAM sorting is unrelated to enrichment background."}

---

## 39. Why can analyzing up- and down-regulated genes separately be useful? {.quiz-question}

- [Opposing biological programs can be obscured when both directions are combined]{.correct data-explanation="Separate directional enrichment can distinguish increased from decreased biological programs."}
- [It makes alignment splice-aware]{data-explanation="Splice awareness is an alignment property."}
- [It changes base quality scores]{data-explanation="Differential-expression direction has no effect on raw sequencing quality."}
- [It guarantees significant enrichment]{data-explanation="Separating directions can improve interpretability but does not guarantee significance."}

---

## 40. Which sequence best represents a defensible RNA-seq interpretation workflow? {.quiz-question}

- [Technical QC → sample relationships → correct contrast → gene-level effects → pathways → biological context]{.correct data-explanation="Interpretation should build from technical validity and sample structure toward gene- and pathway-level biological conclusions."}
- [GO enrichment → FASTQ QC → alignment → experimental design]{data-explanation="This reverses the logical order of the analysis."}
- [Volcano plot → sequencing → RNA extraction → hypothesis]{data-explanation="The workflow should begin with the biological question and experimental design."}
- [Adjusted p-values → library preparation → sample metadata]{data-explanation="Statistical results occur after experimental and computational processing."}

# After the Quiz

## How to interpret your score

::: {.takehome-card}
### Suggested workshop interpretation

**85–100%** — strong conceptual readiness for the hands-on sessions  
**70–84%** — good foundation; revisit the weaker sections  
**50–69%** — review alignment, counting and statistics before the practical  
**Below 50%** — revisit the conceptual deck before moving to Shell/R implementation
:::

The important goal is not memorizing terminology.

It is understanding **why each step exists, what information it produces, and how errors propagate into downstream interpretation**.
